doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Learning jazz in schools versus on the road
summary: They discuss how jazz was once learned by listening and playing in bands, while students now study it in courses and seminars with few chances to perform.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: I think they mentioned, the two of them this morning, some of the big differences. There’s a lot of the young musicians who spend a lot of time in colleges and learn very technically and so forth, and they have to learn what to do with it later on. Which in the earlier days, when people were mostly listening from records and then getting into the situations and playing in the traveling bands, that hearing things was—either you developed it or you were gone.
They had a lot of good places to let that develop.
Like you have to feel it. Because I’m sure when Clark Terry was coming up there were no courses in jazz. But now you go to school to learn jazz.
And he teaches it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

Yes. And you go to seminars for the weekend to learn jazz. They do that in England. I have a great friend who is a retired doctor who loves piano, but never sort of got the hang of jazz. He plays wonderful music, but he goes to seminars in England to learn jazz. But like you say, that’s sort of something that I always thought had to come from inside you, that you made up for yourself.

Yes. It apparently does but it also, as you mentioned, the young students don’t have as much opportunity to get out and actually do it in front of people. I mean there are great college bands, and there are some terrific players out there, it’s just a little harder for them to really get —to take all those skills and then put them into real life.

Well as you say there are a lot of colleges that have fine, fine big bands. The one in North Texas State or wherever it is down there, and there’s one in Colorado and there’s one in Las Vegas, and somewhere, I forget where, they have a big contest every year with all these bands. But what do the kids do when they get out of there?
Where do they develop their skills?
